chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Basir (1) said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Regarding the woman performing Tamattu' Hajj, if she enters the state of Ihram while pure, then menstruates before completing her Tamattu', she performs Sa'i but does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure; then she completes her Tawaf, and her Tamattu' is complete. And if she enters Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'i nor Tawaf until she becomes pure.'

So he (peace be upon him) clarified in this report the correctness of what we mentioned, because he said: 'If she entered Ihram while pure, she performed Sa'i; and if she entered Ihram while menstruating, she did not perform Sa'i nor Tawaf.' If the meaning were not what we mentioned, there would be no difference between the two states. The difference exists because when she enters Ihram while pure, her menstruation may occur after completing Tawaf or while she is in the middle of it; at that time, it is permissible for her to advance Sa'i and make up what remains of Tawaf. But if she enters Ihram while menstruating, she has no way to perform any part of Tawaf, so Sa'i is also withheld for that reason. And this is clear, and praise be to Allah.
And that which indicates that it is permissible for her to perform Sa'i if she finishes Tawaf or has performed part of it, even if she is menstruating, is what has been narrated:

key_terms.أَحْرَمَتْ: She entered the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a woman's Hajj rituals if she menstruates during Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to clarify the procedural validity of Hajj rituals when menstruation interrupts the performance of Umrat al-Tamattu'. The scholar highlights the logical distinction: if a woman enters Ihram pure, she may perform Sa'i and complete the remaining Tawaf after purification, whereas if she enters while already menstruating, she must delay both until purification, ensuring the ritual sequence remains intact.
